page: Amazon Web Services i8g.12xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and a bundled local storage capacity of 11250 GB delivered via NVMe SSDs. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 28 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores reaching the top tier. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, with uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks ranking in the top tier at 404.61 GB/sec and 201.28 GB/sec respectively. Database operations, evaluated via Passmark, also place in the top tier, while Redis SET operations achieve 98.01 million operations per second.

While multi-threaded and memory-bound operations perform exceptionally well, single-core CPU benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, register in the average tier. Additionally, LLM text generation for smaller models is relatively weak, though text generation for medium and large models remains strong. Qualitatively, the high local NVMe storage density and top-tier memory bandwidth provide high resource density for data-intensive workloads, offsetting the moderate single-core speeds.

This hardware profile is suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks. The combination of high-capacity local NVMe storage and top-tier memory bandwidth supports workloads requiring rapid data access and high-volume transaction processing.
